title: Double up

brief.story: The soft-start on the bench fan comes on too quickly: R1 (4.7 kΩ) and C1 (100 µF) give it half a second. The box has more 100 µF capacitors, and the client wants about a second.
brief.goal: Make the voltage at column 14 reach 63 % in 0.85–1.1 s while SW1 is held.

hints: τ = R × C = 4.7 kΩ × 100 µF = 0.47 s. You need about twice that, without changing R1.
Capacitors in parallel add up (the opposite of resistors): two 100 µF side by side are 200 µF.
Fit a second 100 µF with its + leg in column 14 and its − leg on ground: τ = 4.7 kΩ × 200 µF = 0.94 s.
debrief: Capacitors in parallel add their capacitance, because together they hold more charge at the same voltage: 100 µF + 100 µF = 200 µF, doubling τ = R × C. Power boards do this constantly, banking several capacitors side by side instead of one big one.
